# ---- Frame rate ----
# The game steps its time by a frame ratio, its base rate / its frame rate, whatever the frame took: frames longer than a vsync played in slow motion. The ratio takes the host's
# frame step instead (MATCH_FRAME_STEP in patches.py, found by its function on any build that keeps it): 1 vsync at 60 fps, 2 when 60 does not hold, so game time = real time
fps_target
# On an iPhone 18 Pro Max (X1.0) the hold sat at 30 fps for 1, 2, 4 then 8 s after short bursts on the CPU side every 1.3-2.3 s at 60 (the GPU under the late line): each probe
# back to 60 held, then the next burst ended its run before the 8 s that count it held, and each failure doubled the waits. burst: such a burst at 60 is paid back without a step
# up (nvn_fstep.h FSTEP_BURST_N); the GPU-bound back-off is unchanged.
# DM_FPS_HOLD_BACKOFF=double in env.txt turns it off. Not yet run on the phone
fps_hold_backoff
# The owner's iPhone 18 Pro Max runs (X1.0): with the hold off the game felt better than with the hold's stays at 30 fps, every frame shown as soon as it is ready. off is the
# launcher's Hold frames default for this game (fps_hold_backoff and fps_resume apply when a player turns it on); DM_FPS_HOLD=on in env.txt turns it back on
fps_hold
# After a trip out of the app (iPhone 18 Pro Max, X1.0, 40 s away) the frame across the stay counted as late and owed 15 vsyncs, which the game ran fast to pay back, and with the
# frames either side three late frames held 30 fps for about a second. on: that frame is on time and owes nothing, and the 30 frames after it pay their lateness back without
# stepping the hold up (nvn_fstep.h nvn_fstep.away). DM_FPS_RESUME=0 in env.txt turns it off. Not yet run on the phone
fps_resume
# A frame stood in the display link's queue nearly all the time on an iPhone 18 Pro Max at 30 fps, a tick (33 ms) more from enqueue to display; the 60 fps run had two or more
# frames waiting on part of the ticks in most windows after its first 3 minutes. 60 ticks in a row with two or more frames waiting drop one (DM_PRESENT_TRIM, which env.txt can
# set, 0 for off): at 30 fps game enqueue to display about 85 -> 53 ms, 9 frames dropped in 2.5 minutes, no smoothness cost seen. Checked only at 30 fps on iOS: the game's
# default 60 fps and the Mac use it untested
present_trim
# Two owner runs on the iPhone 18 Pro Max (X1.0, hold off, one with present snapshots and one without): snapshots helped a little, the swapchain texture free once its copy ran
# (nvn_mtl.m mtl_snap_on). The launcher's Frame buffering defaults to it; DM_PRESENT_SNAP=0 in env.txt turns it off
present_snap
# In the slow windows of the X1.0 iPhone runs the 'NVN queue replay' thread ran its ~60 M instructions a frame at 1.6-2.0 GHz (12-13 ms of CPU) against 3.9-4.3 GHz (5-6 ms) in the
# fast ones; it and 'dm-encode' had QoS user-interactive alone, no frame deadline. on: each declares a time-constraint policy sized to its own CPU time per frame (nvn_rt.h,
# hle_nvn.c nvn_rtw_tick). DM_REPLAY_RT=0 in env.txt turns it off. Not yet run on the phone
replay_rt
# About 20 command nodes a frame against 4 spare command copies (the queue line's 'command nodes without a spare copy' about 20 a frame), and about 6 new pool tables of about 312 KB a
# frame against 16 spares, all in flight. on: 32 copies (16 MB in all) and 64 tables, the newest table dropped when every spare is in flight (nvn_queue.inc nvn_replay_spares,
# nvn_mtl.m pool_table_give). DM_REPLAY_SPARES=0 in env.txt turns it off. Not yet run on the phone
replay_spares
# Each save load makes a 12288x12288 Depth16 (296 MB) and a 4096x4096 Depth32F, zeroed by a clear-only render pass: on an M3 Pro that pass failed with
# kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorOutOfMemory and took the queue with it in about half the loads (NXNative PR #2306), and the owner's iPhone 18 Pro Max logs show a GPU frame of
# 145-158 ms after it. on: such depth textures are zeroed by copies from the zero buffer (nvn_mtl.m tex_zero_fill, port of NXNative 4cdd5577), and the log's 'depth zero:' line gives
# the GPU time of the upload batch that zeroed it and of that frame and the next two. DM_DEPTH_ZERO_COPY=0 in env.txt turns it off. Not yet run on the phone
depth_zero_copy
# A pool table keeps two lists of IDs to take again at the next change, and past 1,024 builds the table whole: upstream's log of this game, streaming an area in behind the pause menu,
# built its texture table whole at nearly every submission (NXNative PR #2389). on: the lists hold 8,192, what one patch takes (nvn_mtl.m pool_ids_max, port of NXNative 034e91a8's
# limit), up to 1 MB more for the lists. The oot4 iPhone run never reached 1,024. DM_POOL_IDS_8K=0 in env.txt turns it off. Not yet run on the phone
pool_ids_8k
# In one heavy area on an iPhone (X1.0) about 800 textures a frame went into the 512-entry table of finalized textures for 300 frames, then about 364, most of them ones it had pushed
# out a frame or two before; each put and eviction sent the pool tables down their patch path (about 465 kept a frame), an estimated 1-4 ms of replay CPU a frame. Every other
# game and run stays under about 100 a frame. A ceiling of 4096 (nvn_mtl.m ghost_cap), drained back to 512 when idle or at low headroom; DM_NVN_GHOST=512 in env.txt takes it back.
# Not yet run on the phone
ghost_table
# Test 3 on an iPhone 18 Pro Max (X1.0, both runs on battery, same build): after the clock drop that follows each save load, the game's threads spent 4.1-5.3 s of CPU a
# 300-frame window in runs of yields with no other work (2.5-5.3 s overall), 43-53 fps, 38-107 frames dropped a window; with storm sleeps 1.2-1.7 s, 45-58 fps, 6-89 dropped,
# and in the opening movie 0.10-0.14 W of CPU power against 0.31-0.36 W at the same 58 fps. sleep: once a worker's yields have run 500 us with no other work, each further
# yield sleeps up to 50 us; the thread that acquires the window texture keeps spinning (hle_thread.c ystorm_note). It does not stop the clock drop. DM_YIELD_STORM=0 in env.txt
# turns it off
yield_storm
# ---- Movies ----
# The movies are AV1 decoded by VideoToolbox. On an iPhone 18 Pro Max (X1.0) iOS ended the hardware decoder while the notification panel was down during the opening movie: every later
# temporal unit failed with -12903 (kVTInvalidSessionErr) and the movie ran through its file in about 2 s, 365 of 9,254 pictures shown. With the key the dead session is dropped and
# a new one starts at the next key frame, the last picture shown until then at the skipped units' times (hle_movie.c movie_vt_restart; DM_MOVIE_RESTART=0 in env.txt turns it off)
movie_restart
# ---- Graphics ----
# agl wraps its clears in render conditions on Donkey Kong Bananza and Splatoon Raiders; the same library here
render_cond
draw_barriers

# As Tears of the Kingdom: the terrain's height, blend and hole maps are written by the CPU into textures after they are created. Without these keys they stay zero: holes in the ground and the wrong materials
tex_flush_upload
tex_dirty_upload
